segment.description: The Calfkiller River, a White County tributary of the Caney Fork rising in Putnam County and flowing south through Sparta to its mouth at the Great Falls Lake/Caney Fork pool. Cataloged with USGS gauge 03419530 (Calfkiller River at Hwy 70 at Sparta); TWRA's stocked reach is the White County river.
segment.boundaries: County spread: White (GNIS 01305600; the cataloged river), headwaters in Putnam; HUC 05130108. Temperature evidence below comes from stations at/below Sparta on the lower-mid river.

coldSource.notes: No cold-water source documented. The catalog's 'spring-fed-ish' characterization is an editorial note without an agency citation. TWRA's Great Falls Reservoir page documents the river's lower reach as musky habitat whose fishing 'is tough [a]s water temperatures rise during the summer' - a warmwater signal for the lower river.

holdover.detail: No agency documentation of holdover either way. TWRA stocks the river only in spring (two seasonal 2026 weeks of 3/22 and 3/29, Rainbow Trout); no summer or winter stocking rows exist, and no creel or sampling evidence of between-stocking survival was found.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documented: the Calfkiller appears in no TWRA trout-regulation category (absent from the wild-trout list and every special-regulation section of TWRA's trout regulations page, checked live this session); the musky/bass fishery TWRA documents for the river's lower reach is warmwater.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: TWRA stocks the Calfkiller only in spring (2 seasonal rainbow weeks in March 2026) and grab samples below Sparta show summer water up to 29.0 C (Jul 1980), with 21.8-25 C typical - warmwater summer conditions with no documented between-stocking survival.
